text: Lazarus Saturday, the thirtieth of March. They came at nine, in a truck, with a paper. They took the bell down at noon. She came down the last of the way on her own and cracked on the frozen ground; I will hear that note until I die. At three they blew the tower. Then they wanted silver, and there is no silver, and they went down into the crypt. The lamp was lit. The young one in the good coat, Volkov, broke the wax on the altar step to show them there was nothing in it. There was. It was wet. Red, not black. A thousand years, and red. I kept the lamp forty years, not to know, but to keep. Now I will keep this book instead.

Palm Sunday. No willows this year; nobody went for them. Three of them are sick: the two who carried it up the stairs, and the one who caught Volkov's glove. The fever came in the night. They shake, and they are thirsty past any thirst I have seen in a man. At first light the brigade left for Staryi Brod, the sick under a tarpaulin in the truck bed, Volkov in the cab with his satchel on his knees. He did not look at me. I think he wanted to. Grach and Avdotya Pakhomova sat with the sick all night in my kitchen, because somebody had to, and they were the two who said so. The bell lies in the yard with her mouth in the mud. The children will not go near her.

Great Wednesday. Grach has the fever. Avdotya has it. The same thirst. I have put them in the house where the others lay, and I sit with them, because now it is my turn to be the one who says so. A carter from Staryi Brod says the three men died on Tuesday in the fever ward, and there is a soldier on the hospital gate. He says typhus. When I told Grach, he said: typhus does not make you thirsty like this. Then he asked what was in the vessel. I said I did not know. He said: you kept it forty years and did not know? I said that was the whole of the keeping. He laughed, and it hurt him.

Great Friday. Grach died at four in the morning, Avdotya an hour after, holding my hand so hard I have the marks. At noon a boy came over the fields from Staryi Brod, not by the road, because the road has soldiers now. He said that in the night the three dead men in the hospital got up. He said it the way a child says a thing he has seen. He said they bit the orderly. He said the soldiers shot at them and they did not mind. I have not told the village. Nobody will touch Grach and Avdotya. So I will. Tomorrow. Under the tower, where the ground is already broken. The fourth day. I have read that chapter two hundred times, and never once from this side of it.

Holy Saturday. I buried them myself under the fallen tower, as deep as one old man can dig in a day, and read over them. At the ford there is a cordon, a machine gun and a board: TYPHUS. The soldiers are boys. One called across the water to ask if we had bread. We have. Pascha. I served it at midnight in the roofless church, and the whole village came, with candles. Christ is risen. I said it and they answered it, and I meant it, and I mean it now, in the morning, with the candles out. Whatever is in the vessel, and whatever lies under the tower, this is still true. I write it down so that I do not lose it. The ground under the tower has not moved. It is the second day.

Bright Monday. The fourth day. They came up a little after dark. I was in the church and heard the rope posts fall. I will not write what they look like; whoever reads this will know, or will not need to. I struck the bell where she lies, with the smithy hammer, because a bell is what the village knows to come to, and they came, running, and I barred the doors from inside. Forty-one of us. The children are asleep on the vestment chests. Grach and Avdotya walked round the church all night, slowly, the way the sick walk, and in the morning they stood at the door and did not try it. They do not try doors. They wait. Lord, I buried them with my own hands and I said the words. The words were right. It is not the words that were wrong.

The eleventh. Three days in the church. They will not come in: a man with a megaphone said twice that the district is closed for typhus and help is coming, and then the megaphone said nothing more. Pyotr Ilyich keeps the count of the days in chalk on the wall, because the fourth day is the only thing now. Oil in the lamp for one more night. We kept it five hundred years and none of us knew what for, and the ones who opened it were not wicked men. Men with a paper and a truck. It only ever needed that. Whoever finds this: it was not the Lord who did this, and not that poor boy in the good coat either, not all of it. It was that nobody was left to keep watch. Keep watch. I am going down to the crypt to fill the lamp, and then I will go out through the church door myself, and Pyotr Ilyich will bar it behind me, so that none of them has to be the one who goes. Remember, O Lord, Thy servant Serafim, and Matvei, and Avdotya, and all of them, by name.
I won't give you the keys. They aren't mine. I only hold them.
Get up, get up, my dears. Not for them, your knees. Go home. Take the children.
Young man. Take the silver. Take the bell. Only don't go down into the crypt.
There is nothing down there that you need. And there is something there that you don't.
What was closed on the fourth day, let no one open.
Arkady. Son. I am asking you. Not for God's sake. For your own.
Confirming the general resurrection before Thy Passion, Thou didst raise Lazarus from the dead, O Christ God.
